terms.gloss: value highly, set great store by
terms.grammar: phrase: aestimō, aestimāre, aestimāvī, aestimātum with the genitive of value (magnī, plūris, plūrimī, parvī)
evidence: Cic. Att. 10.1.1: per enim magnī aestimō tibi firmitūdinem animī nostrī et factum nostrum probārī
terms.comment: The genitive says how highly: magnī, plūris (more), plūrimī (most), parvī (little). Aestimāre alone is to estimate, to value at a price (Lewis & Short).

terms.grammar: phrase: faciō with the genitive of value
evidence: Cic. Fam. 15.14.2: quem jam diū plūrimī faciō
Cic. Fam. 3.4.2: duo enim duārum aetātum plūrimī faciō
terms.comment: Common of people: aliquem plūrimī facere, to think the world of someone.

phrases.latin: per enim magnī aestimō tibi firmitūdinem animī nostrī et factum nostrum probārī
phrases.english: for I value it very highly that you approve of my firmness and of what I did

phrases.latin: prīmum ut tē, quem jam diū plūrimī faciō, tantō intervallō vidērem
phrases.english: first, to see you, whom I have long thought so highly of, after so long

sources: Lewis & Short: aestimo · Lewis & Short: facio
